metaDescription: Tow-behind leaf vacuums compared: engine-driven suction versus ground-driven sweepers, impeller design, bag capacity and mower or tractor fit.
expertTake: The Agri-Fab Hard Top Mow-N-Vac is the best tow-behind vacuum here for its 32 cubic foot hopper and 54-inch deck compatibility, the Agri-Fab Soft Top is the value pick, and the SuperHandy towable is the high-horsepower alternative with a one-hand dump. Skip the sweeper-style unit if your yard is mostly wet oak leaves: brushes pack and stall.
introParagraphs: A tow-behind leaf vacuum turns your tractor or zero-turn into a leaf collector. A separate engine spins a fan and an impeller that pull leaves and clippings in through a hose, shred them and blow them into a large bag or hopper that rides behind you, so you collect while you mow or sweep.

Not every tow-behind collector works that way. Some rely on a hose from the mower deck, others carry their own engine, and sweeper types use ground-driven brushes. The difference decides capacity, wet-leaf performance and what machine you need in front. This guide compares those designs and what to check before buying.

products.name: Agri-Fab Hard Top Mow-N-Vac 32 Cu Ft 208cc
products.description:
Agri-Fab's Mow-N-Vac pairs its own 208cc engine with a hose that connects to your mower deck, so the mower cuts and the vacuum collects the clippings and leaves. A claimed suction speed up to 80 MPH moves debris through the hose to the hopper. The hard top version holds 32 cubic feet, about 26 bushels, which means fewer unloading stops than any soft bag here.

It is designed for decks up to 54 inches, with templates and zero-turn guidance included. That wide compatibility is what makes it the top pick: most owners have one of the common deck sizes. A hard top resists weather and keeps its shape, which helps when you tip the load.

The tradeoffs are cost and bulk. It is the largest and priciest of the Agri-Fab pair, and you need space to store a trailer-size collector. Change the engine oil each season, clean the intake hose and check the impeller for dings after sticks. Because the hopper rides behind the mower, a full load adds real drawbar weight, so test on a slope before committing to a steep yard.
products.bestFor: Large lawns with a 42 to 54 inch deck mower and lots of leaf fall.
pros: 32 cubic foot hard-top hopper cuts unloading stops
cons: Highest price tier of the Agri-Fab pair
Needs a compatible mower deck and discharge

products.name: Agri-Fab Soft Top Mow-N-Vac 29 Cu Ft 208cc
products.description:
The Soft Top uses the same 208cc engine and 80 MPH suction claim as the Hard Top, with a slightly smaller 29 cubic foot, 220-gallon fabric collection system. A universal deck adapter and a 126-inch by 6-inch clear hose fit right-hand discharge decks, so you can see when the hose clogs.

The soft top is lighter and folds smaller for storage, but fabric wears and holds less than the hard top. The capacity difference of three cubic feet is modest, so the real distinction is durability and price tier.

For a typical suburban acre it is the sensible buy. Check the hose for cracks each season, empty the fabric bag fully and let it dry before storage. Plan the compost or curb location so that dumping does not mean towing a heavy bag far across wet ground.
products.bestFor: One to two acre yards where price and storage space matter.
pros: Same 208cc engine as the Hard Top
29 cubic foot soft top is lighter and folds smaller
Lower price tier than the Hard Top
cons: Fabric wears faster than a hard top

products.name: SuperHandy Towable 15HP 180 Gallon Vacuum
products.description:
SuperHandy takes a more aggressive approach: a 15 horsepower engine with electric start driving a 16-inch serrated impeller, which shreds as it vacuums. That is roughly twice the horsepower class of a 208cc engine, and the impeller diameter is the largest in the group.

A 180-gallon bag is smaller than the Agri-Fab hoppers, but a one-hand dump design empties it in seconds without detaching parts, which saves real time over a day of leaf work. The pin hitch connects to a tractor or zero-turn drawbar.

The cost is price and engine complexity. A 15 HP engine burns more fuel and needs more service, and the brand has a thinner dealer network than Agri-Fab. It suits heavy leaf fall on big properties. Keep a funnel and fresh fuel on hand, since a large engine drinks a lot of gasoline over a full afternoon.
products.bestFor: Large properties with heavy leaf fall and a tractor to pull it.
pros: 16-inch serrated impeller shreds as it collects
cons: Higher fuel use and service needs

products.name: SuperHandy Truck Loader Leaf Vacuum 15HP

specList.label: Mount
specList.value: Truck hitch bar or tailgate hanger

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Loads debris into a truck or trailer

products.description:
This is a cousin to the towable, not a collector with its own bag. The same 15 HP engine and 16-inch serrated impeller sit on a frame that mounts to a truck hitch bar or tailgate and blows shredded leaves straight into the bed.

For crews who haul leaves away, a loader skips the middle step of dumping a bag. For a homeowner it is overkill, since you need a truck and a place to unload.

Compared with the towable, it moves debris faster to a final destination but has no onboard storage. Expect commercial engine maintenance and keep the hose clear. Make sure your truck's hitch rating and bed height suit the loader before ordering.
products.bestFor: Crews and large properties that haul debris away by truck.
pros: Serrated metal impeller shreds on the way in
cons: Requires a truck and a disposal site

products.name: YINTATECH 42-Inch Tow-Behind Sweeper 20 Cu Ft
products.description:
This is not an engine-driven vacuum. A ground-driven brush sweeps leaves and grass into a 20-cubic-foot hopper as the wheels turn, with an adjustable brush height and a full-enclosure cover that keeps debris from splashing out.

The benefit is simplicity: no engine, no fuel, no impeller to jam on sticks. The limit is wet leaves and heavy mats, which pack against the brush, and it will not shred. It is the sensible choice for dry autumn leaves and pine needles on flat ground.

Compared with the Agri-Fab vacuums it holds less and cleans less aggressively, but it costs far less and has almost no upkeep. Set the brush just touching the turf rather than pressed into it, since a low brush scuffs grass and wears fast.
products.bestFor: Dry leaves and needles on flat lawns where simplicity and low cost matter.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Engine-driven vacuums like the Agri-Fab Mow-N-Vac pull debris through a hose and chop it. Ground-driven sweepers like the YINTATECH brush it up with no engine. Vacuums handle wet leaves and clippings better, sweepers are simpler and cheaper. A simple test is to ask whether your fall leaves are usually damp; if yes, buy a vacuum, not a sweeper. Sweepers also leave grass and leaf fragments behind on rough turf, where a vacuum lifts them from the surface in one pass.

A 208cc engine drives the Agri-Fab pair and a 15 HP engine drives the SuperHandy units with a 16-inch serrated impeller. A bigger engine and impeller shred and move more, but burn more fuel and need more service. Remember that a bigger engine also adds weight to the towing setup and vibration to the frame. A smaller engine is perfectly adequate if your leaves are dry and light, and it will start easier on a cold morning.

The Agri-Fab Hard Top holds 32 cubic feet, the Soft Top 29, the YINTATECH 20 and the SuperHandy towable a 180-gallon bag. More capacity means fewer stops, but also more weight to tow when full. Think about where full bags go, because capacity only helps if you can unload where the leaves end up. Soft bags compress under weight while hard tops keep their shape, which makes dumping cleaner on the Hard Top.

A Mow-N-Vac fits specific discharge sides and deck widths up to 54 inches, so check your discharge. Truck loaders need a hitch bar or tailgate. Confirm before buying. Measure your deck discharge side and width, and compare against the maker's fitment list before ordering. If your deck has a left-hand discharge, you may need an adapter or a different model entirely.

Dump design decides how long each unload takes. The SuperHandy's one-hand dump empties in seconds, while fabric bags take pulling and shaking. Over a day, it adds up. If you empty the load by hand every time, expect a fabric bag to take several minutes of shaking. A fast dump is worth real money if you unload a dozen times each fall.

Clear hoses, as on the Soft Top, let you see jams. Wet leaves, sticks and acorns are the usual cause. Keep the engine off and the impeller stopped before clearing. A clear hose is a quiet advantage, since you can spot a clog before the engine strains. After wet work, rinse the hose and let it dry to keep mold and leaf paste out of the next season.

specDecoder.meaning: Two ways to state hopper size. One cubic foot is about 7.5 gallons. A bushel is about 1.24 cubic feet, so 26 bushels is roughly 32 cubic feet. That means a 32 cubic foot hopper holds about 240 gallons.
specDecoder.watchFor: 29 cubic feet is about 217 gallons, matching Agri-Fab's 220.

specDecoder.meaning: Air speed in the hose, a maker claim. It decides how well the unit lifts wet leaves. Real suction falls as the hose lengthens or bends.
A fan with toothed edges that shreds as it moves debris. It reduces volume. Serrated edges also increase noise.
A drawbar connection secured by a pin. It suits tractors and zero-turns with a hitch plate. Check the drawbar height against the hitch plate. Pin sizes vary, so confirm yours before buying.
A starter motor and battery that replace the pull cord. It matters on large engines. It also reduces the pull effort on a cold, stiff engine. Electric start needs a battery that stays charged.

howWeEvaluated.title: Collection design
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated engine-driven vacuums from the ground-driven sweeper and weighed wet-leaf capability. The Agri-Fab pair led. Wet-leaf performance was weighted heavily, because that is where cheaper collectors fail first. We also noted that sweepers lose ground on rough turf and uneven edges.

howWeEvaluated.title: Engine and impeller
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the 208cc Agri-Fab engine with the 15 HP SuperHandy and its 16-inch serrated impeller. We noted that engine reserve under a clogged hose matters, since jams happen in real use. Fuel use per hour was considered, since large engines add running cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and emptying
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 20 to 32 cubic feet of hopper space and dump designs, including the one-hand dump. We converted gallons and cubic feet to a common unit before comparing hoppers. Weight when full was treated as a handling factor, since towing a heavy hopper downhill needs care.

howWeEvaluated.title: Compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at deck sizes, discharge sides and hitch types, since fit is the main purchase risk. We treated fitment as a purchase risk and flagged models with narrow compatibility. Compatibility notes on the listings were read closely, and incomplete ones were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated the Soft Top as the value pick from the Hard Top as the overall pick. Owner feedback patterns on hose clogs shaped the scoring. Several of these brands are newer, so support access influenced the final order. Return policies and warranty paperwork were included where listed.

cards.label: Vacuum
cards.text: The Agri-Fab and SuperHandy units use engines to pull and shred. They handle damp leaves and clippings but cost more and need upkeep.

cards.label: Sweeper
cards.text: The YINTATECH uses ground-driven brushes, with no engine to service. It struggles with wet leaves and does not shred.

howToChoose.note: Pick a vacuum for wet, heavy fall and a sweeper for dry leaves and needles.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for strong suction, a serrated impeller and a large hose. Wet leaves clump and jam narrow tubes.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Agri-Fab pair claims 80 MPH suction, and the SuperHandy's 16-inch serrated impeller shreds wet material best.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if leaf fall is heavy over several acres, which points to the Agri-Fab Hard Top or SuperHandy towable.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if leaves are light and dry. The YINTATECH sweeper does the job at a lower price.

maintenance.why: Dusty leaf work is hard on small engines. Fresh oil protects bearings.
Sticks and acorns dent blades and cause vibration.

faq.q: Can I use a tow-behind vacuum with a zero-turn?
faq.a: Many fit, but check the discharge side and deck size. Agri-Fab includes templates and zero-turn guidance.
A vacuum handles wet leaves and clippings and shreds. A sweeper is simpler but best for dry debris.

faq.q: How big a hopper do I need?
faq.a: For an acre of trees, 29 to 32 cubic feet reduces stops. Smaller yards can manage with less.
Only small ones. Large sticks damage the impeller or jam the hose.

faq.q: How do I clear a clog?
faq.a: Stop the engine, wait for the impeller to stop and clear by hand with care or with a tool.

faq.q: What do I do with the shredded leaves?
faq.a: Compost them or spread a thin layer on beds. Thick layers smother grass.
